title: On the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa modules of the maximal multiple Z_p-extensions

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: References [1] through [9] are cited in the paper body (e.g., [1] Bouw et al. in Lemma 4.1.1, [2] Dodson in Lemma 4.1.1, [4] Fröhlich in Proposition 2.2.1, [5] Fujii in Introduction, [6] Fujii in Lemma 2.1.3 proof, [7] Fujii throughout, [8] Fujii in Introduction, [9] Fukuda in Introduction) but their full bibliographic entries are absent from the reference list. The bibliography begins at [10]. For [1]-[6] and [9], no entries exist at all. For [7] and [8], entries are also missing (the bibliography goes [10]-[32]). This is a formal error preventing readers from locating cited works.

The proof of Lemma 4.1.7 states: 'Define K ↔ ⟨I₁, I₁, I₂, I₂⟩'. The inertia group I₁ appears twice in the list. The intended notation is almost certainly ⟨I₁, Ī₁, I₂, Ī₂⟩ (inertia groups of p₁, p̄₁, p₂, p̄₂ respectively), as the argument concerns a p-extension unramified outside {p₃, p̄₃} and the subsequent computation uses ⟨I₁, I₁, I₂, D₂⟩ = ⟨γ, y, xᵃzᶜ, x⁻ᵇ⁻ᶜzᵃ⁺ᵇ⟩ which is consistent with using four distinct inertia groups. The duplication of I₁ could mislead readers attempting to follow the proof.

The text contains OCR processing notes: 'Here is the corrected, ordered OCR text:' (line 370) and 'Here is the corrected text as requested:' (line 604). These are metadata artifacts from the document conversion process, not part of the original paper. Their presence indicates the markdown was produced via OCR, which introduces risk of transcription errors in mathematical notation throughout. For example, some subscript characters and mathematical symbols may be incorrectly rendered.

Reference [8] is cited as 'S. Fujii, On the Iwasawa lambda-invariants of Zp-extensions of an imaginary quadratic field, J. Math. Soc. Japan 62 (2010) 267-294'. Web searches for this paper by title, author, journal, and year returned no matching results. While Satoshi Fujii has other verified publications in Iwasawa theory, this specific citation could not be confirmed. Note: Reference [7] by the same author has a title discrepancy — cited as concerning 'imaginary abelian number field' but the confirmed publication concerns 'imaginary quadratic fields'.

summary: This paper classifies CM-fields k decomposed completely at an odd prime p such that the unramified Iwasawa module X(\tilde{k}) is trivial. The mathematical content appears logically coherent and follows standard Iwasawa theory techniques building on work by Minardi, Itoh, and Fujii. However, the verification identified several issues requiring correction: (1) References [1]-[9] are cited throughout the paper but their bibliographic entries are entirely absent from the reference list, which begins at [10]. This is a formal error preventing readers from locating cited foundational works by Bouw, Dodson, Fröhlich, Fujii, and Fukuda. (2) A notation error in Lemma 4.1.7 duplicates I₁ in a field definition where four distinct inertia groups are intended. (3) OCR processing artifacts at lines 370 and 604 indicate the document was generated via OCR, introducing risk of mathematical transcription errors. (4) Reference [8] (Fujii, JMSJ 2010) could not be confirmed through web search. Key citations to Greenberg, Jaulent, Minardi, Okano, Washington, and Neukirch were verified as authentic. The main theorem (Theorem 1.1.1) is internally consistent as a classification result.
